Use Brisk-S · reasoning low · 1 retry (J): the cheapest configuration to clear the 97% pass-rate gate, though only by 0.1 points.

It costs $0.302 per 1k calls, least of the five that clear, but a fresh run of today's size reads it below the gate 38.6% of the time. If the gate must clear with confidence, high reasoning (L) is the pick, at $0.633 per 1k calls.

!
Confidence: Low.
  • Pass rate is cleared on a point estimate. If J's true pass rate sits below the gate, which its clearance of 0.1 points cannot rule out, then L is the cheapest configuration that clears; settling J four times in five would take 111,255 cases, two-sided.
  • The pick is the best of several candidates. J's figure is partly the luck of being picked from 18 configurations: a run on fresh cases tends to read it lower, which pushes it toward or under the gate and leaves L, with 1 points of room, as the pick.
  • No arm is the control. Only for a claim that one configuration beats another on pass rate: every gap here is read unpaired and so wider than a paired reading; the call rests on each configuration's own gate reading and its cost.
  • Cost routing unknown. Only if another provider's pricing for Brisk-S or Atlas-M reorders them: the snapshot names the model each arm served but no provider, so every cost is this run's routing's, not the model's own.
RecommendationShip Brisk-S · reasoning low · 1 retry (J). It reads 97.1% against the 97% gate at $0.302 per 1k calls, the least of any configuration that clears: about $1,208 a month if the declared volume counts calls, more if it counts tasks, by each arm's calls per task.
Why not the othersBrisk-S · reasoning high · 1 retry (L) clears with more room, 98%, but costs $0.633 per 1k calls, $1,324 more a month if the volume counts calls. Every Atlas-M that clears costs more again; the best, Atlas-M · reasoning high · 1 retry (F), reads 98.6% at $3.477 per 1k calls. No Nano-XS configuration clears; its best, Nano-XS · reasoning high · 1 retry (S), falls 2.2 points short.
WatchThe weakest margin is the pick's own: Brisk-S · reasoning low · 1 retry (J) reads 97.1% on Pass rate against 97%. A fresh run of today's size reads it below the line 38.6% of the time, against 0.9% for L, and as the best of 18 it likely reads high.
NextShip J now; in parallel the planner's owner declares whether the gate must clear on its interval. If it must, switch to L.

What you could change

What you could changeWhat it decidesWhat happens as it moves
The pass-rate gate's thresholdWhich configuration is the cheapest that clearsJ stays the pick for a gate above 95.3% up to 97.1%; L from there up to 98%; Atlas-M · reasoning high · 1 retry (F) up to 98.6%; above that nothing clears. Lower gates admit cheaper Brisk-S and Nano-XS configurations.
Reading the gate on the interval rather than the point estimateWhether J counts as clearingJ's computed interval crosses the gate while L's sits above it, so on the interval L becomes the pick at $0.633 per 1k calls against $0.302; a month that is $1,324 more if the volume counts calls, more if it counts tasks.

Next steps

  • The planner's owner declares whether the gate must clear on its interval or on its point estimate. Whether J ships or L does: more cases cannot practically settle J, which would need 111,255 cases to settle four times in five, two-sided.
  • Add worked multi-hop examples to Brisk-S's planning prompt, where J reads 95.6% (a figure with no stated case count, so no interval), then re-run J on 1,660 fresh cases. Whether the change lifts J clear of the gate at its current cost: a run that size settles a clearance as large as L's, 1 points, four times in five; a smaller lift needs more cases.
  • Re-run L on 1,660 fresh cases. Whether L's clearance survives fresh cases. The size assumes today's estimate of 98%; the best-of-many selection likely reads that high, and a lower true rate needs more cases to settle four times in five.
  • Declare each task's traffic share and case count, and whether the monthly volume counts calls or tasks. Whether the overall pass rate reflects the production mix, and what the step from J to L costs a month.

Left out, and why

Latency
No latency gate was declared, and latency does not reorder the two Brisk-S options; full figures in the appendix.
Calls per task
Varies little between the options a decider would weigh and changes no gate reading; it matters only to what a month costs if the volume counts tasks, which the cost lines say.
Extra calls per task and outcome
The snapshot holds no figures for either.
Per-task pass rates of the other configurations
The gate reads overall; per-task figures state no case counts, so they are leads, kept in the appendix.
Model and reasoning lever effects across Atlas-M and Nano-XS, and the high-reasoning retry move for Brisk-S
They explain why other configurations fall short or cost more but do not change the pick; all are in the appendix.

Method

Cases
Each configuration ran 1,200 cases once each across the task types; none was lost or failed to run. Per-task case counts are not stated.
Pass
The input does not define what makes a planner run pass.
The gate
Pass rate at least 97%, declared before the run and read on each configuration's point estimate, as declared.
Intervals
Computed here from each configuration's cases as a binomial spread by the normal approximation, at the level each block prints. Gaps between configurations are unpaired, since no control was run, and uncorrected for the number of comparisons. Run sizes are quoted two-sided, sized to settle four times in five unless a table says otherwise.

Caveats: No arm is the control.

Cost
Cost per 1k calls as measured. Each arm names its model but no provider. Monthly figures use the declared volume of 4,000,000 read as calls; the input does not say whether it counts calls or tasks, and if it counts tasks each monthly figure grows by the arm's calls per task.
Selection
The pick is the cheapest of 18 configurations to clear the gate, so its pass rate likely reads high.
Source
Synthetic example data from docs/eval-report-kit/references/r2-config-sweep.json, run 2026-10-23.
